messages:
novuscare_csec: Hey team — we found unexpected KMS decrypts for our NovusCare private deployment around 2026-02-18T02:12:xxZ. 3 decrypts from principal svc-ingest-novus from IP 45.77.12.9. We didn't authorize any ingest change. Please advise urgently.

anna_support: Thanks for flagging — escalating to security. Can you paste the log snippet or message id? Also which KMS provider (customer-managed AWS KMS / GCP KMS / HSM)?

novuscare_csec: Customer-managed AWS KMS, key alias arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222333:key/abcd-ef01. Snippet below (sanitized):

```
2026-02-18T02:12:07Z INFO kms.decrypt requestId=xyz-123 principal=svc-ingest-novus region=us-west-2 ip=45.77.12.9 resource=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222333:key/abcd-ef01
2026-02-18T02:12:12Z INFO kms.decrypt requestId=xyz-124 principal=svc-ingest-novus region=us-west-2 ip=45.77.12.9
2026-02-18T02:12:46Z INFO kms.decrypt requestId=xyz-125 principal=svc-ingest-novus region=us-west-2 ip=45.77.12.9
```

anna_support: got it. tagging @leo_sec. :rotating_light:

leo_sec: Looking. First-pass: we need to confirm whether svc-ingest-novus is a Redwood-managed service account or customer VM role. @mike_infra can you check the tenant binding and any recent RBAC changes?

mike_infra: pulling cluster audit. Quick grep shows a RoleBinding creation at 2026-02-18T02:06:51Z: user alice.ops created clusterrolebinding "svc-ingest-novus-binding" granting cluster-admin to serviceaccount:ingest:svc-ingest-novus.

leo_sec: Hmm — cluster-admin grant 6 minutes before the decrypts. That matches timing. Do we have the Kubernetes audit entry for who executed the create? Mike, paste the audit line.

mike_infra: audit snippet: "verb":"create","user":{"username":"alice.ops@novuscare.com","uid":"u-9012"},"objectRef":{"resource":"clusterrolebinding","name":"svc-ingest-novus-binding"}"

anna_support: NovusCare says alice.ops is an ops engineer but claims they did not run that command. Could be compromised.

leo_sec: Next steps (containment):
- Disable the service account token (patch SA to remove secrets / add an annotation to disable). Example: `kubectl -n ingest patch sa svc-ingest-novus -p '{"secrets":[]}'`
- Revoke any short-lived credentials tied to that SA and rotate AWS KMS data key encryption keys (DEKs).
- Block egress from worker pool to AWS KMS endpoint if possible (security-group firewall) to stop further decrypts.
- Snapshot logs and take forensic copy (preserve S3/KMS CloudTrail entries).

mike_infra: Executed SA patch and added network ACL rule to block 45.77.12.0/24 outbound to kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com. I also pulled kube-apiserver audit bundle to /tmp/novuscare-audit-1778459999.tar.gz (shared via secure link).

deploy-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-0473 | sev=high | owners=@leo_sec,@mike_infra | link=https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-0473

novuscare_csec: Appreciate the quick action. We see decrypts stopped after 02:13:10Z.

leo_sec: Good. Forensics notes: KMS logs show principal ARN `arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/svc-ingest-novus-role` performing Decrypt. The role was assumable by a federated user tied to alice.ops credentials — possible credential compromise or internal misuse. We need CloudTrail full session context and MFA logs for alice.ops.

anna_support: NovusCare asked whether Redwood had any backend key access — we do not. This is BYOK customer-managed; our integration uses KMS proxy in the private control plane but does not hold plaintext. Confirmed.

leo_sec: Action items (short-term):
- NovusCare: rotate alice.ops credentials and enforce MFA immediately.
- NovusCare: rotate/deprecate the KMS key (generate a new key version and rewrap DEKs).
- Redwood/mike: preserve all audit logs, and export CloudTrail event IDs for decrypts.
- Redwood/leo: run privilege review and alerting: add rule for any ClusterRoleBinding create granting cluster-admin outside of scheduled change windows.

mike_infra: Exported CloudTrail entries and S3 object keys to the incident ticket. Also created saved query in our observability: `aws.kms.decrypt where principal=svc-ingest-novus and eventTime >= \"2026-02-18T02:00:00Z\"`

novuscare_csec: We're rotating creds now. One question: will rotating the KMS key break Redwood data access during rotation for private deployment?

leo_sec: Short answer: there will be a brief window where older DEKs can't be decrypted if you immediately disable the key. Recommended procedure: create a new key version and re-encrypt DEKs before disabling old key. We can coordinate with you on a maintenance window; Redwood's runtime supports key rotation but we'll need to update key ARN in config. I'll open a runbook and step through it with your ops.

anna_support: From support side — logging note: enable audit-bridge retention for at least 90 days for this tenant.

leo_sec: Post-incident actions (PIA):
- For NovusCare: RBAC hygiene, restrict service accounts to least privilege, remove cluster-admin grants for SA.
- For Redwood: add an automated check flagging service account rolebinding grants that grant cluster-admin or equivalent in private deployments (detect and notify).
- Add KMS decrypt anomaly alert (cross-region decrypts, new principal, unusual IP ranges).
- Add a playbook for BYOK customers that includes immediate KMS key rotation steps and sample commands.

mike_infra: Note: we found an older terraform change in the repo that had accidentally allowed a wide assume role. Opening PR to tighten trust policy. PR link: https://git.internal/novuscare/infra/pull/532

novuscare_csec: Thanks — we're scheduling a 30-min call in 15 to walk through rotations. Can Redwood join?

leo_sec: Yes, I'll join. Quick ask before the call: send us the full CloudTrail request IDs (xyz-123/124/125) and the kube-apiserver audit tarball link. We'll bring the rotation checklist.

anna_support: Follow-up: creating support ticket SPT-2026-1894 for the coordination and attaching incident notes.

novuscare_csec: Uploaded CloudTrail IDs to the ticket and granted Redwood read access to the audit S3 prefix.

leo_sec: Final temp containment summary: SA token disabled, network egress rule applied, decrypt activity stopped. Severity remains high until creds and KMS rotations complete. We'll update timeline after the rotation call. :white_check_mark:

novuscare_csec: Confirmed rotation finished at 03:05Z, keys rewrapped, and access validated. We'll keep this thread updated if anything else shows up. Thanks for the quick help.

leo_sec: Closing loop: will run a 24-48h monitoring sweep, add the RBAC alert, and produce a short PIA doc attached to the incident ticket.

anna_support: Marking support ticket SPT-2026-1894 as engaged and linking to incident INC-2026-0473.

deploy-bot: INC-2026-0473 status -> monitoring (owner=@leo_sec).
